'''Ama Kazukime Shrine''' (海士潜女神社, Ama Kazukime Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Kuzaki Town|ja|国崎町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzaki Town|1=Kuzakichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11146786}}, {{ill|Toba, Mie|en|Toba, Mie|qid=Q819629|lt=Toba City|1=Toba, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}. It was formerly known as Ama Gozen (海士御前) until 1869. While not under the administration of {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}, it maintains a deep connection to Ise and enshrines the legendary {{ill|ama (female diver)|ja|海女|lt=Ama diver|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ama (female diver)|qq=}} Oben, attracting faith from divers across Japan.
Ama Kazukime Shrine enshrines the legendary ama named Oben, who dedicated an abalone to Emperor's Princess, Yamatohime-no-mikoto. The shrine is regarded as having divine favor in preventing dizziness during diving and is worshiped by local amas and divers nation-wide.<ref>https://www.bing.com/ck/a?!&&p=5de8780f388380bac94109889b3b4851fbe31c06bec1a4e2bc67168448801156JmltdHM9MTc0MzYzODQwMA&ptn=3&ver=2&hsh=4&fclid=0baff627-1adb-6b49-298a-e3e31b796a0d&u=a1aHR0cHM6Ly9xcnRyYW5zbGF0b3IuY29tLzAwMDAwMDE3NDcvMDAwMDAx&ntb=1</ref>
== Overview ==
The {{ill|Honden|en|Honden|qid=Q2044994|lt=honden|1=Honden}} of the shrine is a wooden structure in {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|1=Shinmei-zukuri}}, while the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=haiden|1=Haiden (Shinto)}} is built in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|qid=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} and surrounded by {{ill|sacred fences|ja|瑞垣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sacred fences|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 玉垣}}. The grounds span approximately 920 {{ill|Pyeong|en|Pyeong|qid=Q706688|lt=tsubo|1=Pyeong}} (about 3,041 square meters). The main deity is Kazukime-no-Kami, identified with the legendary ama Oben. She is revered as the progenitor of ama divers, offering protection against dizziness and marine hazards. The shrine is also a pilgrimage site for divers across Japan.
== History ==
In the 26th year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}} (4 BCE), {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} visited Kuzaki while searching for offerings for the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}. Oben presented abalone, which impressed Yamatohime and was subsequently dedicated to Ise. This marked Kuzaki’s selection as one of Ise’s {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|lt=Kanbe (social class)|lt=Divine rice fields|ja|神戸 (民戸)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/divine rice fields|qq=}}. The shrine was renamed Ama Kazukime Shrine in 1869 and later consolidated 17 smaller shrines between 1906 and 1907.
== Rituals ==
=== Hachiman Festival ===
Originally the festival of Hachiman Shrine, it centers around archery rituals held on {{ill|January 5|en|January 5|qid=Q2202|lt=January 5|1=January 5}}. Key rituals include the "Manabashi" ceremony, where chosen men prepare fish with chopsticks and knives without touching it by hand.
=== Two Boat Festival ===
Held annually over three days in November, this festival involves competitive boat races between the Kuzaki subregions of Satodani and Kaimadani. Participants offer fish and {{ill|Omiki|en|Omiki|qid=Q3313722|lt=omiki|1=Omiki}} at the {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} during the race, believed to predict the year’s fishing fortune.
=== Mikazuki Ritual and Grand Festival===
Historically, this ritual involved female divers from seven villages gathering on the lunar calendar's June 1 to dive for abalone. Although discontinued in 1871, the ritual has been periodically revived for commemorative occasions, such as the 2016 G7 Ise-Shima Summit.

== Subsidiary Shrines Enshrined Together ==
The Amamochime Shrine enshrines the following 17 shrines, which were merged into it in 1906 and 1907. All of these shrines originally held no specific Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qid=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.<ref name="th3">Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): pp. 980–982.</ref>

=== Tsurugi-no-Miya Shrine ===
Tsurugi-no-Miya Shrine (剱宮社) was originally located on Tsurugi Cape. It was merged into Amamochime Shrine in 1906 (Meiji 39). It is also known simply as Tsurugi Shrine.<ref name="kk4"/> According to legend, one of the {{ill|Imperial Regalia of Japan|en|Imperial Regalia of Japan|qid=Q327465|lt=Three Sacred Treasures|1=Imperial Regalia of Japan}}, the {{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|lt=Kusanagi Sword|ja|草薙剣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusanagi no Tsurugi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天叢雲剣}}, which sank during the {{ill|Battle of Dan-no-ura|en|Battle of Dan-no-ura|qid=Q968676|lt=Battle of Dan-no-ura|1=Battle of Dan-no-ura}} alongside Emperor Antoku, was retrieved from the sea by a monk named Ajari Enjo and subsequently enshrined there.<ref name="kk4"/>
== Festivals ==
Amamochime Shrine is home to two major festivals in Kunisaki Town: the Hachiman Festival and the Two Boats Festival.<ref name="sg63">Shimamoto (1994): p. 163.</ref>
=== Hachiman Festival ===
Originally dedicated to the Hachiman Shrine, this festival centers around an archery ritual held on January 5th.<ref name="sg63"/> Hachiman Festivals are widely celebrated in fishing villages across Toba City, emphasizing prayers for bountiful catches and maritime safety.<ref>Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): p. 809.</ref> 
The festival includes:
* '''"Hatsuyori" (January 2nd):''' Preparatory meetings for the archery ritual.<ref name="sg63"/>
* '''"Daikon Kaki" (January 4th):''' Households prepare the offerings for the next day.<ref name="sg63"/>
During the festival, participants perform the {{ill|Manabashi Ritual|ja|真名箸神事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manabashi Ritual|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, in which fish is filleted into sashimi using chopsticks and knives without touching it by hand.<ref name="th9">Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): p. 809.</ref>
=== Two Boats Festival ===
The Two Boats Festival (二船祭) takes place over three days in November.<ref name="tt">Toba Tourism Association "[http://www.toba.gr.jp/200/post_523.html Two Boats Festival]" <[https://megalodon.jp/2013-0421-1742-58/www.toba.gr.jp/200/post_523.html Web Archive]> (accessed April 21, 2013).</ref> The highlight is a boat race between the Kaima and Satodani communities, representing prayers for abundant fish catches.<ref name="sg63"/> 
== Surroundings ==
The shrine is located in Kunisaki Town, near the center of Toba City. Visitors can take the Kamome Bus from the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=JR Sangu Line|1=Sangū Line}} Toba Station to the Kunisaki stop, followed by a 7-minute walk.<ref name="cv"/> Note that there is no dedicated parking space nearby.<ref name="cv"/>
